doc.radial: show_labels=false makes every radial icon-only so Steam never substitutes modifier glyphs such as Ctrl, so the icons within one radial (ring and centre) must differ. A radial is ring slots touch_menu_button_1..20 plus an optional centre, touch_menu_button_0. fire_type 1 is Steam's button release: rest a thumb on the left pad, slide to an icon, click the pad and the slot fires when that click is released; lifting the thumb without clicking fires nothing. haptic_intensity is the tick each button gives, as on Steam's own radials. A slot names an action, which types its chord, or one of pages, which switches Steam to the layout preset whose id it names (controller_action CHANGE_PRESET with the page's label and icon, as community radials on the Deck bind their Back centres, workshop item 3372611329). The default preset puts quick_slots on the left pad: Save, Load, Previous Slot, Next Slot, Next Bezel, Next Shader, Settings, Menu, Screenshot and Quit, with an empty centre so a click released in the middle fires nothing. Settings switches to the settings preset, whose left pad is settings_slots: Next Bezel, Bezel On/Off, Next Shader, Shader On/Off, Fit (the next of the four Fit states, integer game, integer bezel, non-integer game and non-integer bezel, live; with no bezel to place, integer game and non-integer game), Aspect (4:3 or 16:9 where a system has both; saved at once, applied by Restart Game), Render Scale (the system's next render scale, native, 2x or 3x where its emulator renders above native; saved at once, live on Dolphin, applied by Restart Game elsewhere), Controller Layout (player 1's next layout where a system has several: Wii Remote, Nunchuk, Classic, GameCube; each press steps on, live where the emulator switches it, GameCube on Wii included; a layout an emulator reads only at boot is saved and applied by Restart Game), Restart Game (restarts the game once to apply what waits for a restart; with nothing waiting it says so and restarts nothing), Players (the Semu menu's page of pads and player slots) and Reset to Default (asks for a second press), with Close Settings in the centre, which returns to the quick radial. No choice restarts the game by itself: its toast says RESTART TO APPLY, and only Restart Game reboots. The settings radial stays until Close, so a slot can be pressed again and Reset's second press lands inside its 3 s window; meanwhile the rest of the controller is the gamepad, and View, the grips and the pointer work as in the gamepad preset. Holding View or an upper grip enters the hotkey preset, whose left-pad radial is menu_slots (Up, Down, Confirm, Back, Bezel On/Off, Shader On/Off, Reset to Default and Players) with Open Menu in the centre; letting go returns to the gamepad preset. Declarative system_layers add held left-pad radials; Semu runs their slots itself. The Wii layer is held with either lower grip (L5/R5, Steam's button_back_left and button_back_right) and declares Wiimote, Nunchuk, Classic and GameCube as slots 0 through 3, each picking that layout for player 1 as Controller Layout would, with Restart Game in the centre, so a layout an emulator reads only at boot is picked and applied without letting go; its Ctrl+Shift+F9..F12 chords stay inside the held layer. No binding may send a key without a modifier: the game receives Steam's keys too, and Esc (ui.escape) exits RetroArch, so the hotkey set's R3 is Menu Back.
doc.quit_chord: The physical View/Menu buttons emit XInput SELECT/START unchanged. window_ms is the maximum verifier interval for the pair; the process-group watcher terminates as soon as it observes both buttons held. Radial and HKB quit press the app.quit chord and Select+Start as well.
doc.controllers: One entry per Steam controller_type Semu ships a template for. vocabulary names the sources and inputs Steam accepts on it (from Valve's own templates for that controller: controller_base/templates and chord_*.vdf) plus how many radial buttons it has; every name a template emits must be in it. layout names the Semu layout drawn on it. neptune is the Deck; triton, the new Steam Controller, uses the Deck's names and gets the Deck layout unchanged; gordon, the 2015 Steam Controller, has no d-pad, right stick or upper grips. Only the controller of the default template names controller_file and configset_file: the Steam Controllers ship as templates, picked once under Controller Settings, because their per-user file names were never observed.
doc.layouts: A layout is presets walked in order (preset 0 is the gamepad Steam starts in). Each preset maps a source to a group kind the renderer draws: face, dpad, left_stick, right_stick, trackpad_stick (the right pad as the right stick, output_joystick 1 as in Valve's gordon template), left_trigger, right_trigger, pointer (Steam's mouse; a soft click is a left click, which DS and 3DS read as a tap), switches, quick_radial, menu_radial, settings_radial, layer_radial and the hotkey_ kinds, which draw the hotkey_bindings and fall back to the plain kind when nothing is bound. held_by lists the inputs (and activator, Full_Press unless named) that enter the preset while held; letting go returns to the gamepad. A preset after the first with no held_by is a page: a radial page (radial.pages) switches to it by its id, it stays until another page switches away, and its holds work as from the gamepad; one that nothing holds and no page names is refused. switches maps each switch input to the XInput button it passes through; grips maps a system layer's activators to this layout's inputs, and a layout without them gets no such layer. gordon: the left pad is the quick radial, the right pad the pointer, holding the left grip makes the left pad a d-pad and holding the right grip makes the right pad the right stick; its settings page is the gamepad with the settings radial on the left pad, as on the Deck.
doc.templates: Exactly one template carries default:true, and it is for the controller with a controller_file and configset_file (the Deck). semu steam input writes every template into templates_dir and the icons into binding_icons_dir, then the default template as each Steam user's controller_file under application_config_dir, and adds "semu" { "autosave" "1" } to that user's configset_file under configset_dir, keeping every other byte (a dated .semu-*.bak first, nothing written when the entry is already there): that entry is what makes Steam load the per-user file for the Semu shortcut instead of its Last Resort template. Steam rewrites configsets when it exits, so without --steam-root the command refuses while Steam runs. Each file is written beside its destination and renamed over it, and symlinked destinations are refused. Under each deprecated_config_ids folder only that controller_file is removed.
doc.binding_icons: Every action and radial page declares a non-keyboard Semu PNG, and every action a binding may send has its own. icons/PROVENANCE.md names each one's source; packaging/steam/render-icons.sh renders the Lucide ones from that table and --check proves every committed icon re-renders at RMSE 0. Legacy VDF bindings encode the icon filename and its two colors as comma-delimited metadata, matching Valve's radial-menu format. Physical Deck acceptance: after semu steam input with Steam stopped, the Semu shortcut loads Semu: Steam Deck - Neptune FULL (controller_ui.txt: Local Selection Path for its App ID, config/semu/controller_neptune.vdf); open the quick radial, Settings from it (and Close back), the held menu radial and the Wii layer and see the 10 + 11 + 9 + 5 declared icons with no Ctrl or key glyphs; activate every quick, settings and menu slot, then verify each Wii mode reaches its Dolphin consumer.
doc.platforms: All destinations lie under ${home}/.local/share/Steam, the same on both Linux targets. semu steam input --steam-root DIR puts the same layout under DIR instead (the tests use a scratch root) and refuses any path that leaves it. ${steam_user} is every userdata directory except 0 and anonymous, so every Steam user gets the default profile and the configset entry.
doc.actions: The complete native input vocabulary. Each action declares its chord, semantic label, and manifest-backed Semu PNG. These entries and hotkey_bindings render only the Steam Input templates; the native keymap and the supervisor read config/input/<target>/input.json, and a contract keeps both chord tables identical. Which emulators honor each action is declared per emulator in config/emulators/<emu>/emulator.json input.actions; ui.menu.{up,down,confirm,back} are consumed by the renderer menu, controller.layout.next, the Wii layer's wii.controller.* picks, ui.players and system.restart are Semu's own (the supervisor switches the emulator's layout, opens the players page or restarts the game), and ui.escape is desktop-only (no binding may send it). This file is shared: the linux-desktop and steam-deck targets name it as steam.input.
